'''Chaitanyamoy Ganguly''' is an Indian nuclear scientist<ref name="INSA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N93-1117 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20150118142504/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N93-1117 | url-status=dead | archive-date=2015-01-18 | title=INSA | publisher=INSA | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015 }}</ref> and a former head of the Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA), credited with many innovations in the field of nuclear material science.<ref name="International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)">{{cite web | url=http://www-atalante2008.cea.fr/home/liblocal/docs/Atalante2008/PDF/Ganguly_modif.pdf | title=International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) | publisher=International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304040618/http://www-atalante2008.cea.fr/home/liblocal/docs/Atalante2008/PDF/Ganguly_modif.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="CGCRI">{{cite web | url=http://www.cgcri.res.in/page.php?id=306 | title=CGCRI | publisher=CGCRI | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="IIT Kanpur">{{cite web | url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/net/Dr.Ganguly.pdf | title=IIT Kanpur | publisher=IIT Kanpur | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304053647/http://www.iitk.ac.in/net/Dr.Ganguly.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="Business Week">{{cite web | url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=62698114&ticker=CCO:CN&previousCapId=379153&previousTitle=CAMECO%20CORP | title=Business Week | publisher=Business Week | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015}}{{dead link|date=April 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He was honored by the [[government of India]] in 2002, with the fourth-highest |publisher=Padma Awards |date=2014 |access-date=11 November 2014 |url-status=dead ==Biography==
Ganguly was born on 31 December 1946<ref name="IAS">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/php/fell_detail.php3?name=Ganguly&intials=Chaitanyamoy&year=31-12-1946 | title=IAS | publisher=IAS | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref> at Shibpur in the Indian state of West Bengal.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" /> He graduated in metallurgical engineering (BE) in 1968 from [[Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur]]) of the [[University of Calcutta]]<ref name="CGCRI" /> and had higher training at the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]], (BARC) Trombay.<ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> His career started with BARC at their Radiometallurgy Division in 1969 where he worked till 1995,<ref name="CGCRI" /> in professional positions and as a faculty member at the BARC training school.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> During this period, he was also deputed to Karlsruhe Research Centre (KFK), present day [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]], Germany, on a fellowship from the International Atomic Energy Agency, for advanced research under D. Vollath<ref name="D. Vollath">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/D_Vollath | title=D. Vollath | date=2014 | access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref> and Klaus Kümmerer<ref name="Klaus Kümmerer">{{cite web | url=http://www.leuphana.de/en/about-us/staff-members/klaus-kuemmerer-engl.html | title=Klaus Kümmerer | publisher=University of Luneburg | date=2014 | access-date=13 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119002954/http://www.leuphana.de/en/about-us/staff-members/klaus-kuemmerer-engl.html | archive-date=19 January 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> on [[X-ray scattering]] technology.<ref name="CGCRI" /> On his return, he obtained a doctoral degree (PhD) from the University of Calcutta in 1980<ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> and had postdoctoral research at [[Forschungszentrum Jülich|Nuclear Research Centre, Juelich]], Germany<ref name="CGCRI" /> as a Humboldt Fellow.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> Ganguly, after returning from Germany, was made the head of the radiometallurgy division of BARC in 1986, a post he held till his move to the [[Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute]] (CGCRI), Kolkata in 1995.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" />

In 1998, Ganguly was made the chairman and chief executive of the [[Nuclear Fuel Complex]] of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] and he stayed at the post till 2004.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Business Week" /> The International Atomic Energy Agency appointed him, in 2004, as the head of the Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Materials Section.<ref name="INSA" /> On his retirement from IAEA in 2009, when [[Cameco|Cameco Corporation, Canada]], reportedly world's largest publicly traded uranium company and the third largest producer of uranium,<ref name="World Uranium Mining">{{cite web | url=http://www.world-nuclear.org/info/Nuclear-Fuel-Cycle/Mining-of-Uranium/World-Uranium-Mining-Production/ | title=World Uranium Mining | publisher=World Nuclear Association | date=July 2013 | access-date=13 January 2015 | archive-date=13 June 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140613033122/http://www.world-nuclear.org/info/Nuclear-Fuel-Cycle/Mining-of-Uranium/World-Uranium-Mining-Production/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> opened its India subsidiary at [[Hyderabad]], he was appointed as the president.<ref name="IIT Kanpur" /><ref name="Business Week" /> After over three years at Cameco, Ganguly moved to the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]], as the distinguished visiting professor and continues to serve the institution in that capacity.<ref name="IIT Kanpur" />

Ganguly is a former president and life member of the Indian Ceramic Society<ref name="ICS">{{cite web | url=http://indianceramicsociety.org/index.html | title=ICS | publisher=ICS | date=2014 | access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref> and a former president of the Powder Metallurgy Association of India.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" /><ref name="PMAI">{{cite web | url=http://www.pmai.in/en/ | title=PMAI | publisher=PMAI | date=2014 | access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref> He has served, as a member, many professional organizations such as the [[Indian Institute of Metals]], Indian Institute of Ceramics (IICERAM), Indian Nuclear Society, [[Institution of Engineers (India)]], Materials Research Society of India and the Indian Society for Non Destructive Testing (ISNT).<ref name="CGCRI" /> He has also served as the editor of the ''Journal of Nuclear Materials'',<ref name="CGCRI" /> a peer reviewed journal for materials research in nuclear science.<ref name="JNM">{{cite web | url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-nuclear-materials | title=JNM | publisher=Elsevier | date=2014 | access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref>

==Legacy==
Ganguly is credited with the establishment of the plutonium fuel laboratory at the Radiometallurgy Division of the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]].<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> His contributions are reported in the development of ceramic and metallic fuels based on [[uranium]], [[plutonium]] and [[thorium]], to be used in the research and power reactors of the organization.<ref name="INSA" /> His research is known to have led to the development of ''plutonium rich mixed uranium plutonium monocarbide fuel'', a world first,<ref name="CGCRI" /> for use with the [[FBTR|fast breeder test reactor]] (FBTR)<ref name="INSA" /> at the [[Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research]] (IGCAR), [[Kalpakkam]], making India the first country to use the fuel in a fast reactor.<ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> The development of ''stainless steel clad plutonium oxide fuel'' for ''Purnima Research Reactor'' at BARC and ''aluminum clad, aluminum-uranium 233 fuel''<ref name="CGCRI" /> for ''Kamini Research Reactor'' at IGCAR are two other contributions attributed to Ganguly.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> He is also credited with the development of other plutonium alloys such as [[Plutonium–gallium alloy|plutonium-gallium]] (Pu-Ga), plutonium-aluminum (Al-Pu) and plutonium-beryllium (PuBe) at R and D levels.<ref name="INSA" />
 
During his tenure at the [[Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute]], Ganguly is reported to have developed a high density lead glass for shielding windows from radiation.<ref name="INSA" /> He has also contributed to the development of:
* variants of laser glass and zero expansion glass which are in use in defence and aerospace industries,<ref name="INSA" /> 
* ''thorium based mixed oxide fuels'' for water cooled reactors,
* ''remotely operable sol-gel microsphere pelletisation'' (SGMP) process used in oxide fabrication, and
* carbide and nitride fuel pellets.<ref name="CGCRI" />

His research findings have been recorded in over 200 scientific papers, published at various peer reviewed journals<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Chaitanyamoy_Ganguly/publications | title=ResearchGate | date=2014 | access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref> and he holds four patents.<ref name="CGCRI" /> He is the editor of two books, ''Nuclear Fuel Fabrication''<ref name="Nuclear Fuel Fabrication">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=93HMYgEACAAJ | title=Nuclear Fuel Fabrication | publisher=Trans Tech Publications | editor=C. Ganguly  | year=1989 | pages=438}}</ref> and ''Advanced Ceramics'',<ref name="Advanced Ceramics">{{cite book | url=http://www.abebooks.co.uk/9780878495474/Advanced-Ceramics-C-Ganguly-0878495479/plp | title=Advanced Ceramics | publisher=Trans Tech Publications | editor=C. Ganguly  | year=1991 | isbn=9780878495474}}</ref> both published by Trans Tech Publication, Switzerland.<ref name="CGCRI" /> He is known to have mentored many students for their masters and doctoral researches<ref name="INSA" /> at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]], [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bengaluru, and [[Osmania University]] and is an accredited guide of MTech and PhD at the [[University of Mumbai]].<ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> He has also participated in the ''IAEA technical cooperation program'' for transfer of technology to the developing countries.<ref name="IIT Kanpur" />

==Awards and recognitions==
Chaitanyamoy Ganguly, a ''Distinguished Scientist'' of the [[Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute]],<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" /> is an elected Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (FASc),<ref name="IAS" /> the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (FNASc),<ref name="IAS" /> [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]] (FNAE)<ref name="IAS" /> and the [[Institution of Engineers (India)]] (FIE).<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> He is also a Fellow of the [[Indian Institute of Metals]], Indian Institute of Ceramics<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IIT Kanpur" /> and [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], Germany.<ref name="CGCRI" /> He has received the [[VASVIK Industrial Research Award]], Indian Nuclear Society Award, [[Indian Institute of Metals|IIM]] Kamani Gold Medal and [[Indian Institute of Metals|IIM]] Binani Gold Medal.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="CGCRI" /> He is also a recipient of the MRSI Medal, D. N. Agarwal Award, Malaviya Award of the Indian Ceramic Society and KCP Award of the Indian Institute of Welding.<ref name="CGCRI" /> He has received the National Metallurgists Day Award of the [[Ministry of Steel]] [[Ministry of Mines (India)|and Mines]] and the [[Government of India]] followed it up with the civilian honour of [[Padma Shri]] in 2002.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Padma Awards" />
